messages:
dmitri: Heads-up — after the APAC NIC flaps last week I'm proposing a short preemptive maintenance for racks r-a3 and r-a4 in apac1. Window: tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC. Plan is: canary 5 nodes, then 10-node batches, staggered 10m between batches. Aim: reboot NIC firmware + kernel microcode. Expect small scheduler churn but no full pool eviction. pinging @infra-oncall for scheduling.

maria_eng: ok on the canary approach. can product shift canary traffic to eu for the first 20m? that'll make the canary signal cleaner. also please add a note about model pins — we should pin high-memory jobs off those racks during the window.

kevin_sre: @dmitri please include kube drain flags: we want graceful pod eviction with a 5m graceful period and follow-up force after 6m. something like:
```
kubectl drain node/r-a3-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --force=false
```
Also I'll pre-warm backfill pools for apac1 to reduce cold-pack starts.

dmitri: thanks @maria_eng @kevin_sre. i'll add model pin list and a canary traffic shift note. canary start at 02:00, if clean move to batches at 02:20. each batch will cordon->drain->reboot->uncordon. hold 15m after each batch for telemetry.

ellie_se: ops question — will this touch dedicated customer pools? some Dedicated tenants are pinned to r-a4. If so we need to notify them 24h in advance and offer an SLA fallback to eu-dedicated for the window.

dmitri: good catch. Dedicated pools on r-a4: tenant ids T-1732 and T-1849. we'll exclude them from automated drain and do manual per-tenant coordination if they opt in for the reboot.

infra-oncall: scheduling note: i can route a temporary capacity buffer from eu-west2 for 06:00-08:00 APAC local peak to absorb any spill, but that's costly (approx 18 GPU-hours). recommend only if canary shows >5% p95 latency regression.

kevin_sre: cost tradeoff: spinning up cross-region bursts will hit on-demand rates ~3x reserved. estimated delta: $2k for a full 18 GPU-hour buffer. opsbot, please post maintenance notice 12h before.

opsbot: Maintenance notice created and pinned in #status-updates: "apac1: NIC microcode preemptive reboots for racks r-a3,r-a4 — 02:00-04:00 UTC. Expected short bursts of scheduler churn. Dedicated tenants on r-a4 will be contacted separately." :bell:

maria_eng: also add a metrics watchlist: p99 latency for text-gen routes, active GPU utilization, queue length, and prefix-cache hit rate. if p99 > baseline + 7% after a batch abort further reboots and rollback.

dmitri: will add watchlist and abort conditions. final checklist: canary run at 02:00, batches start 02:20, 10m stagger, 15m hold after each batch, dedicated excludes manual coord. backups: cross-region buffer if p95 regression >5% (cost ~ $2k). tagging owners: @maria_eng (product canary), @kevin_sre (drain tooling), @infra-oncall (routing/capacity). anyone object?

ellie_se: no objections. i'll prepare the customer outreach for the two dedicated tenants.

kevin_sre: i'll run a dry-run of the drain commands on a test rack at 22:30 UTC and share logs.

dmitri: thanks team. I'll update the opsrun doc and post final notice at +12h.
